output_text:
name: dotnet-msix
Package .NET desktop apps as MSIX from csproj (`WindowsPackageType`) or WAP projects; sign, distribute via Store/App Installer/SCCM/Intune, configure updates, bundles, and CI/CD. Assumptions: Windows App SDK 1.6+, Windows 10 build 19041+ (1709+ for App Installer auto-update), .NET 8.0+.
For WinUI setup/mode comparison: [skill:dotnet-winui]. AOT: [skill:dotnet-native-aot]. CI/CD: [skill:dotnet-gha-patterns], [skill:dotnet-ado-patterns]. NuGet: [skill:dotnet-nuget-authoring]. Containers: [skill:dotnet-containers]. Samples: [references/detailed-examples.md](references/detailed-examples.md).

WinUI 3/Windows App SDK can package directly from `.csproj`; WPF/WinForms use a Visual Studio “Windows Application Packaging Project” WAP (`.wapproj`, not standard `Microsoft.NET.Sdk`) referencing the app project.

Build:
dotnet publish --configuration Release --runtime win-x64 \

All MSIX packages must be signed to install on Windows. The signing certificate's Subject must match the `Publisher` attribute in the package manifest.

Development certificate/signing:
$cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate `
-Subject "CN=My Company, O=My Company, L=Seattle, S=WA, C=US" `
-FriendlyName "MyApp Dev Signing" `
-CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My" `
-TextExtension @("<REDACTED_IP>={text}<REDACTED_IP>.<REDACTED_IP>.3", `
"<REDACTED_IP>={text}")
$password = ConvertTo-SecureString -String "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" -Force -AsPlainText
Export-PfxCertificate -Cert $cert `
-FilePath "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
$signtool = Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin\*\x64\signtool.exe" |
Sort-Object { [version]($_.Directory.Parent.Name) } -Descending |
Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
& $signtool sign /fd SHA256 /a /f "MyApp_DevSigning.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

Production direct distribution: obtain a trusted CA certificate (DigiCert, Sectigo, GlobalSign); Subject must match the `Publisher` in `Package.appxmanifest`; timestamp signature for long-term validity.
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /sha1 "THUMBPRINT_HERE" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
& signtool.exe sign /fd SHA256 /f "production-cert.pfx" `
/p "$env:CERT_PASSWORD" `
/tr http://timestamp.digicert.com /td SHA256 `
"AppPackages\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"

Store re-signs packages during ingestion; development cert is replaced with Microsoft-issued cert. No production signing certificate is needed for Store-only distribution. Development/enterprise may use self-signed certs (manually install/deploy); direct download requires trusted CA.

Store workflow: register at https://partner.microsoft.com/dashboard, reserve app name, build with Store association:
dotnet publish --configuration Release --runtime win-x64 \
Submit the `.msixupload` file through Partner Center; Microsoft validates, signs, publishes.

App Installer (`.appinstaller`) supports direct distribution/auto-update from web server, share, or CDN. Configure package identity/version/URI and update options (`HoursBetweenUpdateChecks`, `ShowPrompt`, `UpdateBlocksActivation`, `AutomaticBackgroundTask`, `ForceUpdateFromAnyVersion`).
ms-appinstaller:?source=https://mycompany.com/apps/MyApp.appinstaller

Enterprise deployment: Intune (cloud), SCCM/MECM (on-prem), Group Policy, PowerShell.
Add-AppxPackage -Path "\\fileserver\apps\MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix"
Add-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online `
-PackagePath "MyApp_1.0.0.0_x64.msix" `

Custom update UI: `Package.Current.CheckUpdateAvailabilityAsync()`. MSIX differential updates download changed blocks automatically when the same `PackageName` and `Publisher` are used.
